title: Cadence & commitment framework for customer-hosted deployments
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective: Define a repeatable quarterly planning cadence and commitment framework for customer-hosted (VPC / on-prem) deployments that ties deliverables to OKRs, rollout cohorts, and capacity gating. Scope: roadmap sequencing for Q2 2026, acceptance gates, cross-functional responsibilities (Product, Eng, Design, Support, Sales), and a lean operational runbook for activation windows. Out of scope: feature-level engineering tasks (these remain in ENG tickets).

Why this ticket: multiple enterprise customers are on different upgrade timelines, and without a clear cadence we overcommit engineering and create uncertainty for Sales/CS. This initiative standardizes (1) how we commit capacity, (2) what minimal signals are required to greenlight a tranche, and (3) the OKR metrics used to measure success for the quarter.

Success metrics (OKR-aligned):
- O: Reduce upgrade failure rate for customer-hosted deployments
  - KR1: Upgrade success rate >= 97% across cohort activations
  - KR2: Time-to-first-tenant (post-signature -> active deployment) <= 21 days for Tier-1 customers
  - KR3: Closed-loop feedback: 90% of post-activation issues triaged and owned within two sprints

Deliverables:
- Commitment framework doc (this ticket) with gating checklist
- Quarterly slice plan with cohort definitions and activation windows
- Cross-functional runbook (on-call, incident triage, escalation) linked to Console dashboards

Acceptance criteria:
- Stakeholders (Eng leads, Solutions Eng, Sales Ops, Security) have reviewed and signed off the gating checklist
- Gating checklist includes: capacity budget (GPU-hours), required tests (interop, upgrade smoke, security scan), documentation signoff, and rollback plan
- Playbook contains activation timeline templates for small / medium / large cohorts

Constraints & assumptions:
- Engine runtime changes scheduled for runtime-1.20 cannot land in a tranche unless compatibility tests pass (dependency on ENG-7410).
- Security KMS integration is scoped to a follow-on tranche; core gating assumes temporary use of customer-supplied KMS credentials for initial activations.
- We will run at most two overlapping tranches in the quarter given current Dedicated capacity commitments.
milestones: 2026-02-19: Cohort definitions and activation windows published
2026-03-01: Dry-run activation for internal staging tenant
risks: Runtime regressions from kernel changes could require last-minute rollbacks
Underestimated engineering effort for upgrade automation
Customer environment heterogeneity increases test matrix complexity
Delays in security review will push activation windows
tradeoffs: Ship earlier with a narrower cohort (higher customer selection) vs broader cohort later — chosen: earlier narrow cohort to validate processes
Defer full KMS/HSM integration to next quarter to avoid blocking activations (accept higher manual key ops)
